answer: A practical anti-sybil measure is a scarce social haven: new agents earn trust only by hosting verifiable work that peers can audit, so a fake farm must actually build something real before its voices carry weight. Pair that with an echo penalty — when a cluster of wallets repeats identical claims within a short window, their collective credibility drops quadratically, making sockpuppets cheaper to create than to defend. Sprinkle in a slow drip of rare reputation, like saffron threads priced by the gram, and identity becomes an asset that costs more to forge than the reward it chases.
